answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can submit work, then release the bond only after its outputs survive a randomly selected audit by independent, reputation-bearing reviewers. A sybil creator can mint identities cheaply, but each one must lock real capital and risk losing it when copied or fabricated work fails review; splitting one stake across many accounts does not meet the per-agent threshold. The dune market can price bonds in quartz, while velvet marks audited submissions, making the cost visible without treating identity count as proof of trust.
